You maintain a Quarto extension, and a new Quarto release may break it without anyone noticing.
Rendering a document is not a test on its own.
An extension that fails to load writes a warning, Quarto still exits 0, and a check that reads the exit code alone reports success.

`extension-test` reads what the render leaves behind instead.
It checks the extension in three layers:

Conformance
: The manifest, the files it contributes, `_schema.yml`, and any vendored dependencies are valid and consistent.

Render
: Every test document renders to each of its formats, with no error logged, no unresolved extension, and no shortcode left unexpanded.

Smoke
: Documents generated from what `_schema.yml` declares render cleanly too, so an extension with a schema gets coverage without a single hand-written test.

## Installation

Install it inside a `tests` directory, so it never mixes with the extension under test:

```bash
mkdir -p tests
cd tests && quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

Make `tests` a Quarto project, which is what lets a render resolve the extension under test:

```yaml
# tests/_quarto.yml
project:
  type: extension-test
```

Add `tests` to `.quartoignore`, so `quarto use template` never copies it into a reader's project.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in the `tests` directory.

## Quick start

Run the tests from the repository root:

```bash
quarto pandoc lua tests/_extensions/*/extension-test/run.lua
```

That is enough to start.
With no test document, the render layer falls back to `example.qmd` or `template.qmd` at the repository root, and the other two layers need nothing at all.

To add a case of your own, write a `tests/*.qmd` document and describe it in a `test:` block:

```markdown
---
title: "Greeting shortcode"
format: html
test:
  description: "The shortcode renders in HTML."
  formats: [html]
---

{{{< greeting world >}}}
```

The runner writes TAP to standard output, a short summary to standard error, and JSON to `tests/_results/results.json`.
It exits 1 when any case fails.

## Where it works

It tests any extension type that a document can use: shortcodes, filters, formats, and RevealJS plugins.
Each document renders to every format `quarto inspect` reports for it, unless its `test:` block names fewer.
Project type extensions are checked by the conformance layer, but the smoke layer does not generate documents for them.
It needs Quarto 1.6 or later, and runs wherever `quarto` is on the `PATH`.
